chapterTitle: FBISE Annual Exam Simulator 07 (FBISE Diagnostic SLO & Physiological Mechanisms Focus)
subject: biology-10

questions.question: Which primary chemical trigger in arterial blood strongly stimulates the medulla respiratory rhythm center to increase ventilation?

options.B: Increase in carbon dioxide (CO2) concentration and associated hydrogen ions

questions.explanation: Chemoreceptors detect rising arterial PCO2 and lowering pH, vigorously signaling the medulla to accelerate ventilation.

questions.question: In the human nephron, where does 100% of filtered glucose and amino acids get reabsorbed back into peritubular capillaries?
questions.explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule utilizes active transport to reabsorb all filtered glucose, vitamins, and amino acids.

questions.question: A resting neuron maintains an electrical resting membrane potential of approximately -70 mV primarily through the active action of:

options.A: Sodium-potassium ATPase pumps (pumping 3 Na+ out for every 2 K+ in)

questions.explanation: The Na+/K+ ATPase pump electrogenically extrudes 3 Na+ ions for every 2 K+ imported, maintaining the resting negativity inside the axon.

questions.question: The visual defect called cataracts is physiologically characterized by:

options.A: Excessive intraocular fluid pressure damaging the optic nerve
options.B: Progressive clouding and opacification of the natural crystalline lens
options.C: Total detachment of the retina from the choroid

questions.explanation: Cataracts involve denatured protein aggregation within the eye lens, causing opacification and progressive loss of vision.

questions.question: How does rheumatoid arthritis fundamentally differ from osteoarthritis in pathophysiology?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune destruction of synovial membranes, whereas osteoarthritis is mechanical cartilage wear
options.B: Osteoarthritis is caused entirely by viral infections
options.C: Rheumatoid arthritis affects only bones of the lower ankle
options.D: Osteoarthritis is cured with simple vitamin A supplements

questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease targeting the synovial membrane, whereas osteoarthritis is degenerative cartilage erosion.

questions.question: In angiosperm reproduction, the female gametophyte (embryo sac) within a mature ovule typically consists of:
questions.explanation: The mature embryo sac contains 1 egg cell, 2 synergids, 3 antipodal cells, and 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei (7 cells, 8 nuclei).

questions.question: A cross between a homozygous red-eyed Drosophila and a homozygous white-eyed fly demonstrates which genetic principle when all F1 show red eyes?

options.A: Complete dominance of the red-eye allele

questions.explanation: The red-eye allele completely masks the white-eye allele in the heterozygous state, manifesting classic complete dominance.

questions.question: In the ecological nitrogen cycle, which chemoautotrophic bacteria oxidize soil nitrites (NO2-) into plant-absorbable nitrates (NO3-)?
questions.explanation: Nitrobacter completes the nitrification cascade by oxidizing nitrites (NO2-) to nitrates (NO3-).

questions.question: Why does continuous fermentation maintain higher industrial productivity compared to batch fermentation?

options.A: Microbes are perpetually maintained in the rapid exponential (log) growth phase
options.B: It operates without any sterility or cooling

questions.explanation: Constant influx of fresh nutrients and extraction of spent media keeps cultures in peak exponential log growth.

questions.question: Penicillin exerts its selective bactericidal action without harming human host cells because:

options.A: Human cells possess thick chitin walls
options.B: Human animal cells completely lack peptidoglycan cell walls targeted by penicillin
options.C: Human cells digest penicillin into glucose
options.D: Penicillin only reacts at 100 degrees Celsius

questions.explanation: Penicillin targets bacterial peptidoglycan cell walls; because animal cells possess only lipid membranes, the drug is selectively non-toxic.

questions.question: How do memory B and T lymphocytes provide long-term active acquired immunity following vaccination?

options.A: They constantly destroy healthy blood vessels
options.B: They persist for decades and rapidly synthesize massive antibody titers upon real pathogen exposure
options.C: They prevent all future DNA mutations
options.D: They replace the red bone marrow entirely

questions.explanation: Long-lived memory cells recognize specific antigens immediately upon reinfection, mounting a rapid secondary immune response.

questions.question: The physiological mechanism where the output of a biological pathway inhibits the initial step to maintain homeostasis is called:
questions.explanation: Negative feedback counteracts deviations from a set point, stabilizing internal physiological parameters within healthy limits.
